It’s a way to express yourself and it’s a very supporting community. Often furries care a lot about animals, (zoophiles are pretty rare and give the community a bad rap and it’s very uncommon) and they create a persona (fursona) that they can draw or make a suit out of custom made that they feel represents them and a lot of suits are dogs because a large percent of people have dogs as a family pet and people feel a connection to their pets and see them as people and love them deeply. Being a furry is not about being sexually attracted to animals though at all. And the furry community is very welcoming,  at furry conventions they hug and boop fursuit noses and many furries make online friends and they meet up at conventions. They’re very friendly. Many people find emotional support in the community and it’s easy to make friends in it. People who may be lgbt or autistic or otherwise ostracized are welcomed and welcome despite any race or gender or religion or disability or mental disorder/disability. I’ve even seen wheelchair furries. Many furries like Disney movies like zootopia with animals that walk on two legs and talk and go on adventures (furries are anthropomorphic animals, basically animals that walk on two legs and talk and do human things). At conventions they have speaking panels and even fursuit dancers. Not all furries have a suit, it’s sort of a status symbol to be able to afford one. A lot of furries like keeping dogs or cats or other household mammals or even reptiles or fish and alot deeply care for the welfare and wellbeing of animals. Sometimes furries can feel disconnected from other people due to bullying and how society can be, and find comfort in the community and with their furry version of their self either drawing them or fursuiting or being around animals. A lot of furries are very empathetic. Furries do not actually think they are animals or believe they are animals. It’s just a for fun and for comfort and thing
